# Hidden choices that change pixels {#sec-hidden}

Reproducing odc-stac's output to the pixel was possible, but only after finding the choices it
makes for you. None is wrong. They just aren't visible at the call site, and each one changes
pixels when it differs from what another tool does.

| Choice | odc-stac / odc-geo | GDAL's own default | Effect when it differs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overviews when downsampling | read (`-ovr AUTO`) | the same in gdalwarp; never through a STACIT VRT | Nearly every value at 20 m → 200 m, by up to 10 dB |
| Overlap merge | first valid wins, in (time, id) order | last wins in a VRT mosaic | Burst overlaps, about 9% of pixels; 449,890 S2 pixels depend on the id tie-break |
| Solar day | one longitude for the whole load (grid centre), whole hours | n/a | 150 IW items at 167°E: 30 groups, against 60 per item |
| Scale/offset | ignored (raw values) | n/a | S2 across baseline 04.00: 6 of 17 groups mix offsets; one offset after the merge is wrong in 1.6-2.3 M of 3.9 M pixels |
| Resample kernel | always `XSCALE=1 YSCALE=1` | widen with the scale | A "bilinear zoom /10" is 2x2 interpolation, not an area average |
| Integer resample nodata | fill value passed as nodata | none | The black SAM input (rasterio ≥ 1.5.1) |
| Multi-band assets | bands counted from `raster:bands` only | the file's bands | Earth Search's 3-band TCI loads as one float32 band; `visual.2` is a KeyError |

In `stacgrid` each of the STAC ones is an argument (`overviews=`, `fuse=`, `grid=` for the
solar-day longitude, `scale=`, `"asset.N"`), with odc-stac's behaviour as the default. That's why
its outputs can be checked against odc-stac pixel for pixel, and why a choice can be changed on
purpose. In the NormCovar port, the resample kernel and nodata are explicit `gdal.Warp`
arguments.

## Write them down

Whichever loader you use, record these at the call site and in the output's metadata:

1. overviews or full resolution;
2. merge order in overlaps;
3. the grouping rule (and, for solar day, which longitude);
4. whether scale and offset were applied, and per item or after the merge;
5. the resampling kernel and its scale;
6. destination nodata;
7. the GDAL version.
